hints: Hint 1: Look closely at the strip structure, the thick walled outer cells are drawn as a thick black line and the thin walled inner cells as a thin line. Ask yourself which side will lengthen more if cells take up water and swell.

Hint 2: Highest water potential means the most dilute sucrose solution, so water will move into cells by osmosis. Think about which side becomes convex (longer) and which becomes concave (shorter) when the thin walled inner cells expand more than the thick walled outer cells.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Observe the strip and the two tissues**
The cut piece has two sides. The outer side has thick walls and stretches very little. The inner side has thin walls and stretches and shrinks a lot.

Remember: thick black line = outer cells, thin line = inner cells.

Step 2: **Recall what highest water potential means**
Highest water potential ($\Psi$) means the most watery, most dilute sucrose solution.

Water moves by osmosis from high $\Psi$ outside to lower $\Psi$ inside cells, so cells take up water and become turgid.

Step 3: **Predict the bending due to uneven expansion**
When water enters, both layers try to lengthen, but the thin walled inner cells lengthen much more.

The longer side must form the outside convex curve, and the shorter side forms the inside concave curve. So inner (thin) outside, outer (thick) inside.

Step 4: **Match to the diagrams**
Only a strongly curled strip with the thin line on the convex outer edge and the thick line on the concave inner edge shows maximum water uptake. That is diagram A, the smile shape with thick on top inside and thin on bottom outside.

options.A: Correct. Thin inner side is convex and longer, thick outer side is concave and shorter. This shows maximum expansion of inner cells after maximum water uptake in the highest water potential solution.
options.B: False. Thin side is still longer than thick side, so some water was taken up, but the curl is only slight. This is a lower water potential than A.
options.C: False. The strip is almost straight, so inner and outer sides are nearly equal in length. This shows little or no net osmosis, close to incipient plasmolysis, not highest water potential.
options.D: False. Thick outer side is convex and longer, thin inner side is concave and shorter. This shows water loss and greater shrinkage of inner cells, so the lowest water potential solution.
